summary: A Sierra National Forest lookout on Signal (Devil's) Peak, in its present form since 1951. Sources disagree on early history and on whether it is staffed or closed today.

facts.design: 14 x 14 ft C-3L hip-roofed wood cab on a tower, in its present form since 1951
facts.status_note: Still standing per the register and the volunteer history page. The latest dated report (2013) says it was closed; current status not confirmed.

staffing.status: disputed: 2010 report says still staffed for fire detection; 2013 page says closed for several years

access.note: Sources conflict. A 2013 page says there is no public access short of hiking. An undated tourism listing describes a dirt road to the summit that a high-clearance vehicle can brave, with places to park partway. Not verified.

visit.trail_note: Hiking reaches the summit. An undated tourism listing also describes a dirt road. Check with the Sierra National Forest before going.

events.note: First structure, a compass lookout, per fire-lookouts.org and Yosemite.com. Peakbagging.com dates its first building to 1911.
12 x 16 ft cabin per fire-lookouts.org. The register dates the octagonal second story to 1911; fire-lookouts.org says 1916.
Octagonal second story added, per fire-lookouts.org (the register says 1911)
14 x 14 ft 4A-R house placed in service per the register and fire-lookouts.org; Peakbagging.com says rebuilt in 1926
Present C-3L cab and tower built in their current configuration
Forest Service repairs: catwalk and door jamb replaced, firefinder refurbished; the 2010 report says still staffed for fire detection
New catwalk and railings; privately funded microwave internet link to Miami Mountain

corrections.why: Spelling error carried over from the register page, which prints 'Marisposa County'. Wikidata and Peakbagging.com both say Mariposa County.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Early dates disagree. The register puts the octagonal second story in 1911. fire-lookouts.org puts the 12 x 16 ft cabin in 1911 and the second story in 1916. Peakbagging.com puts a building in 1911 and a rebuild in 1926. Every source that dates the present cab gives 1951.

Elevations differ: register 6,867 ft (2,093 m); Wikidata 6,965 ft; Peakbagging.com 6,992 ft; fire-lookouts.org 7,079 ft. The record keeps the register figure. The spread may reflect different points or sources.

The 2010 and 2012 entries on fire-lookouts.org describe staffing and renovation, while its 2013 summary says closed for several years. The undated Yosemite.com listing describes an active lookout. No dated source after 2013 was found, so the story does not choose.

notes_for_editor: Current status is the main gap. The newest dated source is the fire-lookouts.org page updated March 1, 2013, which contradicts its own 2010 and 2012 entries. The Yosemite.com listing is undated and the Peakbagging photo caption is from 2002. Check the Sierra National Forest before publishing. The county correction is a spelling fix. The brief's 'built 1951' is the present cab, not the first structure; consider noting the 1900 origin in the record.
